races.title: State House, District 118
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: James M. (Jimmy) Rogers
cands.bio: Jimmy Rogers is a lifelong Haywood County resident who runs Haywood Tractor Company, his family's business. He served more than two decades on the Haywood County school board for the Clyde District and on the Clyde Planning Board. He beat incumbent Mark Pless in the 2026 Republican primary.
cands.gaps: We could not find any stated position or documented action by Rogers on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, growth and land conservation, immigration or H-1B, policing, guns, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. His campaign site speaks only in general terms about fiscal responsibility and local decision-making. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey. We found no news coverage of controversies, no documented foreign ties, and no notable endorsements. We could not find his birth date or when any of his school board votes were taken.

local.label: Roots 100: His campaign website says he was born and raised in Clyde, NC, and has lived in Haywood County all his life.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: He has run Haywood Tractor Company, founded in 1952 by his father and grandfather, since taking over in 1987. He served more than 20 years on the Haywood County school board (Clyde District), including work on finance and policy matters, and several years on the Town of Clyde Planning Board.
qual.why: Long local elected service and small-business management fit the middle band. He has no record in the state legislature and no policy or law career.

cands.name: Danny E. Davis
cands.bio: Democratic candidate for NC House District 118. Attorney and former North Carolina district court judge (30A and 30B districts) who retired in 2010, including six years as chief district court judge. Later chaired the Haywood County Board of Elections. Ran for House District 119 in 2012.
cands.gaps: We could not find where or when Danny Davis was born, or when he moved to North Carolina; his roots score rests on his campaign's statement that he was raised in Western North Carolina. We found no record of legislative service. We found no specific statements from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, land buying by investors or foreign owners, immigration and H-1B, police pay, guns, abortion, or school vouchers and teacher pay raises. His campaign site speaks only in general terms on schools, housing, public safety and taxes. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey. The sources give different lengths for his judicial service, and we could not settle which is correct. We found no controversies, foreign ties or notable endorsements.

local.label: Roots 90: His campaign site says he was raised in Western North Carolina and is a lifelong resident who raised his family there; his birthplace is not given.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Attorney, then North Carolina district court judge in the 30A and 30B districts (retired 2010, six years as chief judge), later chairman of the Haywood County Board of Elections; lost the 2012 Democratic primary for House District 119.
qual.why: Long law career and an elected judgeship fit the middle range, but no legislative service or budget work is documented.
qual.label: Long law career and an elected judgeship fit the middle range, but no legislative service or budget work is documented.
